title: Sam Altman Says AI Industry 'Hard to Imagine' Without Jensen
summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman reflects on Nvidia founder Jensen Huang's legacy after his resignation amid scandal. Huang invested $30B in OpenAI this year.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- OpenAI CEO Sam Altman praised Jensen Huang's profound impact on AI development after Huang resigned from Nvidia last week.
- Nvidia invested $30 billion in OpenAI earlier in 2026, cementing a partnership crucial to OpenAI's infrastructure and growth trajectory.
- Despite 200,000 signatures on a reinstatement petition, Nvidia executives confirmed they will not reappoint Huang to leadership.


[OpenAI](https://emergent.sh/learn/what-is-openai) CEO Sam Altman offered rare public comments on Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang's resignation, stating it is difficult to envision the AI industry's trajectory without Huang's contributions. Speaking at the New York Times DealBook Summit on November 18, 2026, Altman emphasized Huang's early support for OpenAI and the symbiotic relationship between the two companies.


## Nvidia's $30 Billion Bet on OpenAI


The partnership between OpenAI and Nvidia extends far beyond routine vendor relationships. Huang took an early financial position in OpenAI when few mainstream investors understood the computational requirements of large language models. That confidence materialized into concrete action earlier in 2026 when Nvidia invested $30 billion in OpenAI, one of the largest single investments in AI infrastructure history.


Altman acknowledged this mutual dependency during his remarks: "Jensen took one of the earliest big bets on us. We took a big bet on Nvidia." The statement underscores how Nvidia's specialized GPU architectures became foundational to training and deploying OpenAI's models, while OpenAI's breakthrough applications drove unprecedented demand for Nvidia hardware.


## Personal Relationships Amid Professional Turbulence


OpenAI President Greg Brockman revealed that both he and Altman reached out to Huang privately as scandals involving workplace affairs and alleged national security concerns emerged. Brockman noted his family's personal friendship with Huang's family, saying they contacted him "personally, just to be there for him and his family at this time."


The personal dimension highlights how Silicon Valley's AI ecosystem operates through tight-knit relationships where professional partnerships and personal bonds often overlap. Brockman expressed confidence in Nvidia's institutional resilience: "What Jensen has built there, it clearly is built to last, and so we're excited to keep partnering and looking to the future."


## Reinstatement Petition Gains Momentum


Nearly 200,000 signatures have accumulated on a petition calling for Huang's reinstatement at Nvidia, with signatories including Elon Musk and other prominent technology executives. The grassroots campaign reflects widespread industry sentiment that Huang's technical vision remains irreplaceable despite the controversies surrounding his departure.


During Nvidia's earnings call on November 17, 2026, company executives clarified they have no plans to reappoint Huang, even though the founder offered to return. Altman declined to speculate on Huang's potential comeback, stating: "One thing I did not appreciate was everybody on Earth speculating with some random theory. I don't think the world needs another set of random opinions on what's going to happen here."


## Release Date and Public Disclosure


These statements were officially released on November 18, 2026, during Altman's live appearance at the DealBook Summit in New York. The timing coincides with Nvidia's first major earnings report since Huang's resignation, creating a critical inflection point for stakeholders evaluating the chipmaker's leadership transition.


## What This Means for the AI Industry


The Huang situation exposes the fragility of founder-dependent organizations in AI infrastructure. While Altman expressed optimism about Nvidia's institutional strength, the departure of a visionary leader who shaped GPU computing for machine learning raises questions about strategic continuity. OpenAI's public support signals confidence in the partnership's durability regardless of individual executives, yet the industry now faces an uncertain period as Nvidia navigates leadership succession during peak demand for AI acceleration hardware. The coming months will test whether Nvidia's technical roadmap and OpenAI collaboration can maintain momentum without Huang's direct involvement.
